title: Beatrix and the Harbor
premise: In 1898, Elodie Lockridge, an apprentice clockmaker hiding under the harbor alias 'Beatrix,' is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock and finds a sealed letter hidden in its case naming the Lockridge family in a smuggling conspiracy they never joined. As magistrates close in and the harbor's victors begin writing their own account of the affair, Elodie must decide whether to stay invisible or place the true record—testimony, ledgers, and the letter itself—into official hands before the evidence ship sails on the morning tide. Betrayed by the mentor who hid the letter, sustained by a loyal dockworker and a rival clockmaker turned ally, Elodie races the tide to file the truth with the harbor clerk, sacrificing the family workshop to save their name. The book ends at dawn: the ship sails without the letter, the record stands, and Elodie, no longer Beatrix, signs their own name to the repair ledger.
about_author: Xanthe Sterling is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing harbor court records along the northern coast. Their fiction is drawn from the marginalia of forgotten ledgers, where ordinary people fought to be remembered accurately.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Elodie Lockridge, apprentice in a failing clockmaking workshop, is sent to the harbor observatory under the alias 'Beatrix' to repair the master clock. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: quiet pride masking the family's precarity and Elodie's careful invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Case Concealed
chapters.summary: Inside the clock's case, Elodie finds a sealed letter bearing the Lockridge name, dated years before, hinting at a harbor conspiracy. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: dread—the discovery that invisibility was an illusion someone maintained for them.

chapters.title: The Clerk of Record
chapters.summary: Elodie consults harbor clerk Ambrose Pell, who explains how records become history and warns that the victors of the coming inquiry will shape the account. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the first glimmer that truth must be actively placed, not merely known.

chapters.title: Tides and Testimony
chapters.summary: Dockworker Sable Ferren, Elodie's only harbor friend, reveals the evidence ship 'Coriolis' will sail on the morning tide carrying documents to the capital's inquiry. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: loyalty offered freely, complicating Elodie's instinct to trust no one.

chapters.title: The Master's Hands
chapters.summary: Elodie's mentor, Master Ivo Lockridge, denies knowledge of the letter too smoothly; Elodie notices his tools moved. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the first crack in filial trust—loyalty to family versus the pull of truth.

chapters.title: Ledgers in the Dark
chapters.summary: Elodie and Sable break into the harbor office at night and copy shipping ledgers linking the Coriolis's cargo to forged Lockridge signatures. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into fear as the conspiracy's scale becomes clear.

chapters.title: A Rival's Precision
chapters.summary: Rival clockmaker Odile Vasse catches Elodie copying documents and, instead of reporting them, reveals her own grievance against the harbor magnates. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: wary alliance born of shared injury; justice outside the law takes shape.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: A magistrate summons 'Beatrix' for questioning about the observatory clock; Elodie realizes someone reported the tampering. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the noose tightening—Elodie's alias is now a liability.

chapters.title: Questions in a Cold Room
chapters.summary: Under interrogation, Elodie gives careful half-truths while realizing the magistrate already suspects the Lockridge name. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: terror managed through craftsmanship—Elodie measures answers like escapements.

chapters.title: Ivo's Confession, Partial
chapters.summary: Ivo admits he hid the letter years ago to protect the family, claiming ignorance of who framed them; Elodie doesn't believe him. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: a mentor's shame; love expressed as concealment, now indistinguishable from betrayal.

chapters.title: The Victor's Historian
chapters.summary: Elodie observes the magnates' hired historian assembling the official narrative, already erasing dockworkers' names. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: cold clarity—history is being written now, in real time, and it will not include them.

chapters.title: Sable's Price
chapters.summary: Sable is beaten by harbor enforcers as a warning; Elodie tends the wounds and understands the cost of loyalty. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: guilt and resolve—Elodie can no longer hide behind another's courage.

chapters.title: The Escapement
chapters.summary: Elodie finishes the master clock repair and, in its mechanism, finds a second hidden compartment with the original forged signature. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the craftsman's triumph turned evidence—the clock itself becomes a witness.

chapters.title: Odile's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odile offers her workshop's presses to print certified copies of the evidence, but demands the Lockridge workshop as collateral if they fail. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: ambition and justice entangled; nothing given freely.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Elodie sorts the family's possessions, deciding what to carry if the workshop is lost, and confronts what the name is worth. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose—inheritance is not property but the record itself.

chapters.title: The Betrayal
chapters.summary: Ivo takes the letter to trade it for his own immunity; Elodie and Sable intercept him at the quay. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: heartbreak at its peak—loyalty and truth finally pull in opposite directions.

chapters.title: Night of Copies
chapters.summary: In Odile's workshop, the three print, certify, and seal the true account, racing the magistrate's warrant. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: solidarity forged in urgency; justice assembled by hand like a movement of gears.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Oath
chapters.summary: Elodie persuades Ambrose Pell to accept the record into the official registry before dawn, at the risk of his office. POV: Ambrose. Emotional beat: a minor man's quiet courage—the law's machinery turned to justice.

chapters.title: Before the Tide
chapters.summary: Enforcers corner Elodie on the quay as the Coriolis loads; Sable and dockworkers form a human wall. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the harbor itself choosing sides—collective loyalty over hired force.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: The Coriolis sails without the letter; the magnates' evidence is gone, and the registry holds the true account. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: exhausted triumph—the race won by minutes, the cost still unpaid.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: The inquiry opens in the capital with Elodie's certified record as its spine; Ivo, stripped of the workshop, leaves the harbor in disgrace. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: bittersweet justice—the name cleared, the inheritance reduced to truth.

chapters.title: Signed in Full
chapters.summary: Elodie repairs the observatory clock one last time and signs the ledger 'Elodie Lockridge,' retiring Beatrix forever, with Sable and Odile watching from the gallery. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: quiet, earned visibility—measuring the world no longer in what can be carried, but in what can be left standing.
